title: The Story Behind the Card: Why Michael Jordan Wore No. 12
excerpt: The first episode of The Story Behind the Card looks at Sam Vincent’s 1990–91 Hoops #223 and the night Michael Jordan wore No. 12.
author: ManCave Sports Cards LLC
metaTitle: Michael Jordan’s No. 12 Jersey on Sam Vincent’s Hoops #223
metaDescription: Why Michael Jordan wore No. 12, how he ended up on Sam Vincent’s 1990–91 Hoops #223, and how to spot the first-series photo.

body.content: Look at the front of 1990–91 NBA Hoops #223. The name at the bottom is Sam Vincent. But right in front of him is Michael Jordan wearing a red Chicago Bulls jersey with a number that doesn’t look right: 12. It isn’t a misprint. The camera caught Jordan on the one night he wore it.
This is Episode 1 of The Story Behind the Card. The companion YouTube Short is titled “Jordan Wore #12 Once — Hidden on a Sam Vincent Card.”

On February 14, 1990, the Bulls were in Orlando to play the Magic. Jordan’s usual No. 23 jersey went missing before tipoff. With no spare No. 23, he took the floor in a spare No. 12 jersey with no name on the back. The Chicago Bulls’ media guide records No. 12 for Jordan on that date, and the NBA’s archival footage shows him playing in it.

The change didn’t slow down his scoring. Jordan put up 49 points, but Orlando beat Chicago in overtime. The card gives you a still image from a game that would be easy to remember for the scoring alone. Instead, the first thing most collectors notice is that unfamiliar number.

body.text: Why It’s a Sam Vincent Card

body.content: Vincent, playing for Orlando, is the player going up toward the basket in the picture. Jordan is the Bull between him and the camera. That’s what makes the card fun to look at: the player whose name is printed on it is making the play, but the player in front of him gives away the date.

If you’re filing this in a set binder, it goes under Vincent at #223. If you collect Jordan appearances, it also fits that project. Both are good reasons to keep it, but a listing that calls it a Michael Jordan card without mentioning Vincent makes it harder to know exactly what’s being sold.

body.text: The Same Card Number Has Two Photos

body.content: According to Beckett’s comparison of the two versions, the first-series card (catalogued as #223A) shows Vincent going up to the basket with Jordan in front. For Series Two (#223B), Hoops used a different photo: Vincent dribbling in a dark Orlando jersey, without the No. 12 cameo. Both carry #223. The photo switch is documented; why Hoops chose to change it is a separate question, and the two cards alone don’t tell us.

If you’re after the Jordan photo, search for “1990–91 Hoops Sam Vincent 223 Jordan 12.” Then open the actual listing photo and make sure you can see the red Bulls jersey with 12 on it. A back photo can confirm the card number, but it can’t tell you which front you’re buying. If the seller only shows the back, look for a clearer listing before ordering.

body.text: The Detail That Makes This Card Worth a Second Look

body.content: The first-series card is readily available, and you don’t need a graded copy to appreciate it. A raw copy with a clear front lets you see the whole story: Vincent going up, Jordan in the foreground, and the number that looks out of place until you know what happened. That’s the idea behind this series. Sometimes the best thing on a card isn’t the name printed at the bottom. It’s what the photographer caught around it.
